LESSON: READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.3 Reading for Comprehension (2 sessions) • Reading pace • Comprehensio
Topic 2.6: Reading for Information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading for Information, part of Reading 2.3 Reading for Comprehension (2 sessions) • Reading pace • Comprehensio in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why is it good to make plans before carrying out an activity? 2. How can we find the meaning of new words in a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. infer the meaning of vocabulary for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. embrace vocabulary building for language acquisition.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension,

   Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. infer the meaning of vocabulary for effective communication,

   Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. embrace vocabulary building for language acquisition.

   Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read texts aloud about making plans and appointments for fun activities,

2. work with peers to pick out vocabulary from the text,

3. build a vocabulary bank based on words identified,

4. work jointly to infer the meaning of vocabulary from context,

5. confirm the meaning of the words from a print or online dictionary,

6. team up to play a language game involving matching vocabulary to their meaning,

7. team up with peers in class to prepare a planning record for fun activities. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read texts aloud about making plans and appointments for fun activities,
2. work with peers to pick out vocabulary from the text,
3. build a vocabulary bank based on words identified,
4. work jointly to infer the meaning of vocabulary from context,
5. confirm the meaning of the words from a print or online dictionary,
6. team up to play a language game involving matching vocabulary to their meaning,
7. team up with peers in class to prepare a planning record for fun activities. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading for Information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is promoted as the learner engages in collective learning when teaming up with peers in class to

prepare a planning record for fun activities

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is enhanced as the learner explores views to infer the meaning of vocabulary

from context.
